title: The Vennbahn, Aachen to Troisvierges on a Borrowed Railway
subRegion: Ostbelgien and the High Fens, Liège Province

bestPeriod.note: The High Fens hold snow and freezing fog into April and the plateau is genuinely cold; September gives the driest surfaces and the heather.

summary: A converted railway from Aachen to Luxembourg at railway gradients, crossing the High Fens, five German exclaves and three countries in 125 km.
hook: The Vennbahn is a Belgian strip of land running through Germany, which is why the map looks broken: five German villages sit as exclaves beside a cycle path that never leaves Belgian sovereignty. It also happens to be the gentlest way to cross the Ardennes, because trains do not climb more than two per cent. Seven days turns a 125 km trail into a proper week by adding the High Fens, two lakes and the Our valley.

snapshot.Base(s): Aachen → Monschau (2 nights) → Bütgenbach (2 nights) → Sankt Vith → Troisvierges
snapshot.Total Distance / Terrain: approx 290 km, roughly 2,100 m cumulative gain; 80% asphalt rail-trail, 20% compacted crushed stone and gravel, gradients almost never above 2%
snapshot.Getting There: Brussels (BRU) → ICE or IC to Aachen Hbf (approx 2h). Return from Troisvierges or Clervaux on CFL line 10 to Luxembourg City, then onward
snapshot.Who It Suits: Riders who want distance without gradient, families with children over ten, and anyone with a taste for absurd borders

itinerary.title: Aachen to Monschau through the exclaves
itinerary.morning: Pick up bikes in Aachen. Velocity Aachen on the Reichsweg hires trekking bikes and e-bikes and knows the Vennbahn well. Start at the Aachen Hauptbahnhof end of the trail and roll south through Kornelimünster, whose abbey and cobbled Benediktusplatz are worth ten minutes.
itinerary.afternoon: From Roetgen the trail turns strange. The trackbed is Belgian territory, so the German land east of it, Münsterbildchen, Roetgener Wald, Rückschlag, Mützenich, Ruitzhof, is cut off as five exclaves. Signposts change country every few kilometres. Asphalt, with crushed stone near Lammersdorf.
itinerary.evening: Drop off the plateau into Monschau, a half-timbered town wedged in the Rur gorge. The descent into town is steep and cobbled, walk it if the panniers are loaded.
itinerary.dayStats: 47 km, +390 m, asphalt with approx 4 km compacted crushed stone.

itinerary.title: The High Fens loop from Monschau
itinerary.morning: A luggage-free day onto the Hohes Venn. Ride via Kalterherberg and Sourbrodt to the Botrange Nature Centre and the Signal de Botrange, at 694 m the highest point in Belgium. The plateau boardwalks are for walkers only; bikes stay on the marked cycle routes and forest roads.
itinerary.afternoon: Continue past Baraque Michel and the Fagne de la Poleur, then descend the Hoëgne valley toward Sart before turning back east. This is the only day with real climbing, and the wind on the plateau does most of the damage.
itinerary.evening: Monschau's Senfmühle mustard mill and the glassblowers on the Marktplatz. Eat Rhenish, Sauerbraten, Reibekuchen, at one of the Rur-bank restaurants.
itinerary.dayStats: 58 km, +620 m, mixed asphalt and gravel forest track.

itinerary.title: Down the Warche to Bütgenbach
itinerary.morning: Rejoin the Vennbahn southbound past Kalterherberg's oversized church and Küchelscheid, crossing into Belgium proper. The trail runs on embankments and through cuttings with the old station buildings still standing at Sourbrodt and Weywertz.
itinerary.afternoon: Detour west to the Robertville dam and Reinhardstein castle, then east along the Warche to the Bütgenbach lake. The dam-top road gives the classic view down the reservoir.
itinerary.evening: Worriken sits on the lake shore. Swim if it is August, otherwise walk the 8 km shoreline path at dusk.
itinerary.dayStats: 42 km, +320 m, asphalt with approx 3 km gravel around the reservoirs.

itinerary.title: Elsenborn, Butgenbacher Heck and the Ourthe headwaters
itinerary.morning: A loop day. North-east across the Elsenborn ridge, open moorland, military training area boundaries clearly marked and to be respected, and down to Rocherath and Krinkelt.
itinerary.afternoon: Return via Bullingen and the Butgenbacher Heck woods on forestry gravel. This is the day to test a gravel bike or an e-MTB if you hired one; the surface is loose and the descents are fun rather than technical.
itinerary.evening: Ostbelgien's German-speaking Community has its own parliament in Eupen and its own beer culture. The Bütgenbach brewpubs pour local Ourdaller and Eifel beers.
itinerary.dayStats: 48 km, +540 m, roughly half compacted gravel.

itinerary.title: Bütgenbach to Sankt Vith
itinerary.morning: Straight down the Vennbahn through Weywertz and Born. This is textbook rail-trail: 1.5 per cent, cuttings, viaducts, and the occasional preserved goods shed. Surface is asphalt with a long crushed-limestone stretch approaching Sankt Vith.
itinerary.afternoon: Sankt Vith lost its railway and most of its old town in the Ardennes offensive of December 1944, and its history museum is direct about it. Short afternoon by design.
itinerary.evening: Sankt Vith eats better than a town of 9,000 has any right to. The dining room at Zur Post is the serious one in the German-speaking Community; book it before you leave home.
itinerary.dayStats: 36 km, +180 m, asphalt with approx 6 km crushed limestone.

itinerary.title: The Our valley and the three-country stone
itinerary.morning: South from Sankt Vith on the trail through Lommersweiler and Steinebrück into the Our valley, one of the prettiest and least visited river corridors in the Ardennes. Burg-Reuland's ruined keep sits directly above the path.
itinerary.afternoon: At Ouren the Our, the German border and the Luxembourg border meet. The Europadenkmal, three stones for the founding states, stands at the confluence. Cross the bridge, ride 300 metres, and you have been in three countries in five minutes. Then climb gently to Troisvierges over the Luxembourg border.
itinerary.evening: Troisvierges, Ëlwen in Luxembourgish, is the end of the Vennbahn and the northern terminus of CFL line 10. Modest, quiet, and the point where all your public transport becomes free.
itinerary.dayStats: 45 km, +420 m, asphalt with approx 5 km gravel in the Our valley.

itinerary.title: Clervaux and the train home
itinerary.morning: Follow Luxembourg's national cycle network south from Troisvierges toward Clervaux, a short and steadily descending run through the Öslek forests.
itinerary.afternoon: Clervaux's castle holds The Family of Man, Edward Steichen's photographic exhibition and a UNESCO Memory of the World listing; entry approx €6. The Benedictine abbey above the town sings Vespers.
itinerary.evening: Board CFL at Clervaux for Luxembourg City, about an hour. Public transport in Luxembourg is free, bikes included where there is space, and no reservation exists to buy.

accommodationStrategy.name: Hotel Horchem
accommodationStrategy.description: On the river in the old town, with a locked bike garage and a small wellness area that earns its keep after the High Fens day. Two nights here means you ride Day 2 unloaded, which is the difference between a pleasant plateau loop and a slog.
accommodationStrategy.booking: two months ahead; longer for the Christmas market weeks, which are not your season anyway.
accommodationStrategy.priceNote: €110-150 per night for two with breakfast

accommodationStrategy.name: Sport- und Freizeitzentrum Worriken
accommodationStrategy.description: Purpose-built for active groups on the Bütgenbach reservoir: bike storage, a hose-down point, its own rental fleet including e-MTBs, and rooms that are functional rather than charming. The location on the water at the trail's midpoint makes the Day 4 loop possible without moving bags.
accommodationStrategy.booking: six weeks ahead, earlier for Belgian school holidays.

accommodationStrategy.name: Hotel Zur Post
accommodationStrategy.style: Small hotel with a serious kitchen
accommodationStrategy.description: A handful of quiet rooms above one of the region's best-known dining rooms, with enclosed parking for bikes. Staying here on Day 5 rather than pushing on to Burg-Reuland lets you eat properly at the one place in Ostbelgien worth planning around.
accommodationStrategy.booking: three months ahead for the restaurant, which fills before the rooms do.

logistics.emergency: 112 works in all three countries. Mobile coverage on the High Fens plateau and in the Our valley cuttings is patchy, do not assume a signal between Baraque Michel and Sourbrodt.
logistics.money: Cards everywhere except some Fens refuges and farm cafés. Ostbelgien shops close Sunday and often Monday; German Sunday closure is near-total.

other.label: Bikes on German trains
other.text: Regional RE and RB services in North Rhine-Westphalia need a bike day ticket, approx €4.50-6.00, no reservation. ICE services require a compulsory bike reservation, approx €9, booked in advance and frequently sold out; the Deutschlandticket does not cover bikes at all.

other.label: Bikes on Belgian trains
other.text: NMBS charges a bike supplement of roughly €4 per journey. Note that Sankt Vith has no station, the line is the path you are riding. The nearest railheads are Gouvy and Trois-Ponts.

other.label: Bikes on Luxembourg trains
other.text: All CFL travel is free, including bikes, subject to space in the marked carriages. There is no reservation system, so a busy Sunday afternoon can leave you waiting an hour.

other.label: Luggage transfer
other.text: Radweg-Reisen and Rückenwind Reisen both run supported Vennbahn itineraries with hotel-to-hotel bag transport, roughly €12-20 per bag per stage, and will sell the transfer without the accommodation if you ask.

other.label: Rental and shuttles
other.text: Velocity Aachen at the northern end, Worriken at Bütgenbach in the middle. One-way rentals need a shuttle back: the Vennbahn office in Sankt Vith keeps the current list of operators running Troisvierges-Aachen bike transfers, typically €45-70 per person with bike.

other.label: Borders
other.text: Schengen means no checks, but three phone networks will hand you back and forth all day. EU roaming applies throughout; German, Belgian and Luxembourgish networks all appear.

other.label: Protected area rules
other.text: The Hautes Fagnes nature reserve has zoned access. Boardwalks and marked footpaths are walkers only, some sectors close entirely during fire risk or bird nesting, and the closure signs are legally enforceable. Cyclists stay on the numbered routes.

proTips: Ride north to south. The Vennbahn climbs steadily from Aachen to the Fens watershed and then falls all the way to Luxembourg; doing it in reverse gives you 60 km of imperceptible uphill into the prevailing wind.

Check the Hautes Fagnes access status on the Wallonia nature portal the night before Day 2. Sector closures during drought or nesting season can force a 15 km reroute and there is no signage until you reach the barrier.
Start Day 2 by 08:30. The plateau builds cloud and wind through the afternoon, and the Botrange view is a morning thing.
Fill bottles in Kalterherberg or Sourbrodt. There is no reliable water between the Fens edge and Weywertz.
At Ouren, cross the Our on the small road bridge rather than following the marked path straight on, it puts you at the Europadenkmal without a backtrack.
Once past Troisvierges, stop buying tickets. Luxembourg's free public transport means you can bail out of any stage onto a bus or train at no cost.

packingNotes: Tyres of 35-40 mm. Half this route is compacted stone and forest gravel; 28 mm road rubber will punish you in the Our valley.
A genuine windproof shell. The Fens plateau at 690 m is exposed, treeless and reliably 6-8 °C colder than Monschau in the gorge.
Front and rear lights: several Vennbahn cuttings and two short tunnels are unlit.
Two litres of water capacity for Day 2, where refills are scarce.
A spare tube plus tubeless plugs; blackthorn hedge cuttings on the Ardennes forestry tracks are the local puncture source.
A paper RAVeL and Vennbahn map, GPS handovers between three national networks drop out in the valleys.
whatCouldGoWrong: **Fens weather arrives without warning.** Freezing fog and horizontal rain occur on the plateau in every month. Fallback: Day 2 is a loop, so turn back to Monschau at Kalterherberg and ride the Rur valley instead; the trail below the plateau is sheltered.

**A Hautes Fagnes sector closes.** Fire-risk closures shut whole zones at short notice. Fallback: the Vennbahn main line itself never closes, and the Sourbrodt-Weywertz section carries you through regardless.

**The one-way shuttle does not exist on your date.** Small operators run Vennbahn transfers seasonally and by demand. Fallback: return by train, Clervaux to Luxembourg City free, then CFL/SNCB to Liège and Aachen with a bike supplement, roughly four hours total.
